trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside (free). Marvel at Gaudí's architecture without paying entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to the Eixample neighborhood's grid streets and explore the local vibe. Head to Bar Calders or a nearby tapas bar on Carrer del Parlament for affordable pintxos and a cold Estrella Damm. Experience the early Barcelona nightlife warm-up at a local bar in Sant Antoni, one of the trendiest yet budget-friendly neighborhoods, just a short walk from Eixample.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick bocadillo (sandwich) at the airport for ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo or slice of pizza near the hotel for €3–6 after check-in.
meals.dinner: Tapas at Bar Calders or similar Sant Antoni bar — pintxos from €1.50 each, budget ~€12–16 including a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) on arrival — it covers all metro and bus rides and saves money over single tickets. August is hot (~28–32°C), so carry a water bottle. Refill at public drinking fountains throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to La Sagrada Família (book tickets online in advance — ~€26 basic entry, or ~€36 with tower access). Arrive when it opens (9:00) to beat the heat and crowds. The interior is breathtaking and unlike any other cathedral in the world. The exterior alone is worth seeing if budget is very tight — free to admire from outside Plaça de Gaudí.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park paths and gardens are completely free and offer stunning city views. Spend 2–3 hours exploring terraces, viaducts, and Gaudí's mosaic benches. Head back toward Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon wander through its charming squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the cool of the evening in Gràcia's lively squares. Join locals for the aperitivo hour (7:00–9:00 PM) at any square-side bar. Then explore the Eixample Esquerra (left Eixample) nightlife strip known as the 'Gayxample' — vibrant, inclusive, and full of affordable bars. Try Zelig Bar or similar for cocktails starting at €7.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at a local bakery or café near the hotel — €2.50–4. Avoid tourist-facing cafés on Passeig de Gràcia.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or in Gràcia — 3 courses with drink for €11–14. This is the best budget dining deal in Spain.
meals.dinner: Affordable dinner at a Gràcia neighborhood restaurant or grab falafel/kebab wraps for €5–7 from a local takeaway.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least 1–2 weeks ahead — they sell out fast, especially in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry sunscreen and a hat for the afternoon outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) via metro (use your T-Casual card). Explore the narrow medieval streets for free — visit the Roman ruins visible through glass panels on Plaça del Rei, the exterior of Barcelona Cathedral (entry to the cloister is free before 12:30 PM on weekdays), and the ancient Plaça de Sant Felip Neri. This is one of the best free architecture experiences in the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down La Rambla toward the waterfront. Visit the Mercat de la Boqueria (free entry) — don't buy food here as it's overpriced for tourists, but the visual experience is incredible. Continue to the waterfront and Barceloneta beach for a swim and sunbathe (free). Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade. Optionally, visit the Barceloneta neighborhood for its authentic local feel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Gothic Quarter or El Born neighborhood as the sun sets. El Born is packed with atmospheric bars and affordable wine bars (bodegas). Try El Xampanyet on Carrer de Montcada for house cava at ~€2.50 a glass. Later, if you want to experience Barcelona's famous nightlife, head to a club in the Port Olímpic area or Razzmatazz (entry ~€12–18, often includes a drink).

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tostada con tomate (toast with tomato and olive oil) at a local bar in the Gothic Quarter — €2–4. A true Barcelona staple.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in El Born or Gothic Quarter — €11–14 for a full 3-course meal with wine or water.
meals.dinner: Grab pan con tomate and a few tapas at El Xampanyet or similar bodega in El Born — budget €10–15 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter streets are maze-like — download an offline map (Maps.me or Google Maps offline). Pickpocketing is common on La Rambla, so keep bags in front and valuables secure. Beaches are free but can be very crowded in August.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Montjuïc. Ride the Funicular de Montjuïc (covered by T-Casual metro card) up the hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (~€14 entry) — a stunning modernist building by Josep Lluís Sert housing Miró's colorful, playful works. Alternatively, visit the free exterior of the Palau Nacional (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya) and enjoy the panoramic views over the city from the terraces — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Montjuïc Castle (€5 entry or free on first Sunday of the month and Sunday afternoons after 3 PM). Enjoy the sweeping views of the port and city. Walk through the Olympic Ring area — remnants of the 1992 Barcelona Olympics including the Estadi Olímpic (free exterior). Head back down via cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€12.70 round trip) for spectacular views, or take the funicular back down to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc — it's one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable dining and nightlife neighborhoods. Carrer de Blai is famous for its pintxos bars where you can eat for €1–2 per pintxo. Graze along the street for a fun, social, and very cheap dinner. Stay in Poble Sec for drinks or head back to Eixample for club pre-drinks.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee at a local café near the hotel or metro station — €2.50–4.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc! Grab supplies from a nearby supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) — bread, cheese, cured meats, fruit — for €5–8 total. Eat with a view.
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — budget €10–15 for a filling and fun dinner with a beer or two.

day_by_day.notes: MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya) offers free entry on the first Sunday of the month and every Saturday after 3 PM — check if this applies to your visit. Montjuïc is very exposed to the sun — go early or late and bring water. The Carrer de Blai pintxos scene gets very lively after 8 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most extraordinary modernista buildings in the world, designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours run from ~€22, or admire the stunning exterior for free. Alternatively, book a morning concert (sometimes cheaper than tours). Afterward, explore the Sant Pere neighborhood's quiet streets and the beautiful Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful alternative to Boqueria, less touristy, free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon for any missed sights or shopping. Visit the free Parc de la Ciutadella — a beautiful green oasis with a monumental cascade fountain (Gaudí helped design it as a student), a boating lake (rowboat rental ~€6/30 min), and a zoo. Perfect for a relaxed final afternoon. Alternatively, revisit Passeig de Gràcia for window shopping and a last look at the modernista architecture. Visit the free Fundació Antoni Tàpies exterior or pop into any of the many design stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — splurge slightly on your last night. Try a restaurant offering Catalan cuisine with a menú del día or an à la carte dinner at a mid-range local spot for €15–25 per person. End the night with a walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia or one final drink at a rooftop bar. The Azimuth rooftop or similar hotel bars sometimes allow non-guests for drinks with a city skyline view.

meals.breakfast: Final Barcelona breakfast — coffee, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or ensaïmada (Catalan pastry) at a neighborhood café — €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día one last time — find a local spot away from tourist areas for the best value, €11–14.
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner — pa amb tomàquet, escalivada, and a glass of local wine at a restaurant in Eixample — budget €18–25 for a satisfying final meal.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next day, pack bags tonight and confirm transport to the airport. Keep your T-Casual card if it has remaining trips — it's valid for 90 days. Consider buying some local products (cava, olive oil, or paprika) from a supermarket as affordable souvenirs. Total estimated budget for 5 days excluding accommodation: €150–220 per person, depending on museum choices and nightlife spending.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport to Eixample hotel approximately 30–40 minutes via Aerobus or metro Line L9 Sud.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's late dining culture with a relaxed dinner in Eixample. Afterward, enjoy a casual walk around the illuminated Eixample grid streets and grab a drink at a terrace bar to soak in the atmosphere.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bocadillo or menú del día at a café near the airport or upon arrival in Eixample (budget ~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — beloved local spot for tapas and montaditos, mid-range pricing (~€20–28 per person). Arrive before 21:00 to avoid long queues.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C typical). Pack light clothing and sunscreen. Book Sagrada Família tickets online tonight for Day 2 if not already reserved — slots sell out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Take the skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Book the tower access add-on for panoramic views. Allow 2–2.5 hours. The basilica is a 15-minute walk or short metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Head to the old city for a self-guided walking tour through the medieval Gothic Quarter. Explore the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the Roman ruins visible through glass floors at the MUHBA. Cross into El Born to admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and browse the boutique-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — Attend a live concert at this breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage modernist concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Check the August program for classical, flamenco, or jazz performances. Dress smart-casual.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try a traditional pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and café amb llet (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet in El Born — classic Catalan tavern with house cava and tapas (~€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Bar del Pla near the Palau — modern Catalan cuisine, mid-range (~€25–32 per person). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter — cobblestones are uneven. Palau de la Música tickets range €20–55 depending on the performance; book via the official website. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter.

day_by_day.morning: Eixample Modernisme Deep Dive — Start with a visit inside Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — both are within walking distance of the hotel. Casa Milà's rooftop is especially stunning in morning light. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Tickets ~€25–30; book online.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Dining — Head to Barcelona's most famous urban beach for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Rent a sun lounger (~€6–8) and enjoy the Mediterranean. Stroll along the Barceloneta promenade and explore the Port Olímpic marina area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for the Nightlife & Rooftop Bar Crawl — Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife in the Eixample district. Start with sunset drinks at a rooftop bar (try the Almanac or Hotel Pulitzer rooftop), then explore the vibrant Gayxample bar scene around Carrer del Consell de Cent and Carrer de Muntaner.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni (10-min walk from hotel) — popular brunch spot with excellent coffee and avocado toast (~€10–14)
meals.lunch: Chiringuito or seafood restaurant at Barceloneta — fresh grilled fish or paella at La Cova Fumada or similar local spot (~€22–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Light tapas dinner before the bar crawl — Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample for wine and charcuterie (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona nightlife starts late — bars fill up after 23:00, clubs after 01:00. Pace yourself. Carry a light jacket for air-conditioned venues. The rooftop bar crawl works best starting around 20:00 for sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood — Visit Gaudí's colorful mosaic park for stunning city views and iconic architecture. Book timed entry tickets in advance (~€10). After the park, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighborhood, exploring its village-like plazas and independent shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Afternoon — Take the cable car or funicular up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art (~€14 entry), then explore the Montjuïc Castle for panoramic harbor views. Descend via the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car for dramatic views.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Fountain of Montjuïc Light Show (free, runs Thursday–Sunday in summer, ~21:30) followed by dinner in the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc — one of Barcelona's most exciting emerging food scenes.

meals.breakfast: Café in Gràcia neighborhood near Park Güell — try a local pastisseria for ensaïmada and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc or a café at the Fundació Joan Miró (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — famous 'pintxos street' with multiple bars offering Basque-style pintxos from €1.50–2.50 each. Budget ~€18–25 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell monumental zone tickets sell out — book at least 2–3 days ahead. The Magic Fountain show schedule can vary; confirm times at barcelonaturisme.com. Poble Sec is a 20-minute walk or short taxi from Eixample.

day_by_day.morning: Sant Pau Recinte Modernista — Visit the stunning Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO-listed modernist masterpiece by Domènech i Montaner just a 10-minute walk from Sagrada Família and easily reachable from Eixample. Far less crowded than other Gaudí sites (~€16 entry). Allow 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Raval & MACBA — Explore the edgy El Raval neighborhood. Visit the Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona (MACBA) for contemporary art (~€12), then browse the vintage shops and record stores along Carrer dels Tallers. Stop at the Mercat de la Boqueria for a final look (avoid buying food here — it's touristy; just browse).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final nightcap — splurge slightly on a memorable last dinner, then enjoy one final drink at a rooftop or terrace bar in Eixample to close out the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Forn de Sant Jaume bakery in Eixample — classic Catalan pastries and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Suculent in El Raval — acclaimed modern Catalan bistro, excellent value lunch menú (~€18–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza or Honest Greens in Eixample for a relaxed, quality farewell dinner (~€20–28 per person) — or treat yourself to Bodega 1900 (Adrià group vermouth bar-restaurant) for a special final meal (~€35–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If departing on August 20, confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Barcelona El Prat airport is 30–40 minutes from Eixample via Aerobus (€6.75) or taxi (~€35). Leave at least 2.5 hours before departure.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow time for landing, baggage claim, and private transfer to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Barcelona El Prat Airport to the hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided stroll through the iconic Eixample grid to admire the Modernista architecture — including Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) facades from the outside along Passeig de Gràcia, just minutes from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Nightlife & Rooftop Bar Crawl — ease into Barcelona's legendary nightlife scene. Begin with cocktails at a chic rooftop bar such as El Nacional or the rooftop of Hotel Majestic on Passeig de Gràcia, then explore the vibrant bars and clubs of the Eixample district, known locally as 'Gayxample,' for a sophisticated first-night experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Late welcome lunch at Parking Pizza (upscale, Eixample) or a quick elegant bite at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved local institution steps from the hotel.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar — a three-Michelin-star avant-garde restaurant in Eixample offering a world-class tasting menu. Reserve well in advance. Alternatively, Lasarte (also three Michelin stars) for refined Basque-influenced cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private airport transfer for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm Disfrutar or Lasarte reservation months ahead — these are among the world's most sought-after tables. Keep the evening relaxed given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Skip-the-Line Guided Tour — start the morning with a premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Opt for tower access tickets for panoramic views over Barcelona. A knowledgeable private guide will illuminate the symbolism and architectural genius of this UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — after lunch, explore Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter and the trendy El Born neighborhood on a self-guided or private-guided architectural walk. Discover the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the stunning Santa Maria del Mar basilica. Browse the boutique concept stores and art galleries of El Born.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — attend a live concert inside the breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage modernist concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight and ornate ceramic mosaics make this one of the most visually spectacular concert experiences in the world. Dress elegantly for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Federal Café (Eixample) — specialty coffee and artisan pastries in a beautifully designed space.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Xampanyet in El Born — a historic cava bar serving tapas and excellent house cava, beloved by locals and food connoisseurs alike.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Koy Shunka — a Michelin-starred Japanese-Catalan fusion restaurant near the Gothic Quarter, offering exquisite omakase menus.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets with tower access well in advance online — they sell out weeks ahead. Check the Palau de la Música Catalana concert schedule and purchase premium seats (front stalls or first balcony) for the best sightlines of the interior.

day_by_day.morning: Private architectural tour of Eixample's Modernista gems — with a private architect-guide, explore the Manzana de la Discordia ('Block of Discord') in depth, including interior visits to Casa Batlló (with the premium 'Magic Nights' experience if available in the morning slot) and Casa Amatller. Continue to Casa Lleó Morera. This immersive deep-dive is perfect for architecture enthusiasts wanting context beyond the surface.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Dining — take a short taxi or e-scooter ride to Barcelona's most iconic urban beach. Relax on a premium sunbed reservation at a beach club such as CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) or W Barcelona's Eclipse Beach Club. Enjoy the Mediterranean sun, sea, and people-watching in style.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the W Barcelona's Eclipse Bar on the 26th floor, offering 360-degree panoramic views of the city and sea. Then transition into Barcelona's world-famous nightlife — head to Opium Barcelona or Pacha Barcelona for a premium nightclub experience on the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hofmann Pastisseria (Eixample) — one of Barcelona's finest patisseries, run by the legendary culinary school, with exceptional croissants and pastries.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — a sophisticated seafood restaurant with a terrace, known for outstanding paella and fresh catch. Alternatively, splurge at Enoteca Paco Pérez (Hotel Arts, 2 Michelin stars) for an extraordinary beachfront fine dining experience.
meals.dinner: Light late dinner or premium sharing plates at CDLC beach club, or a full dinner at Bestial — a stylish Italian restaurant with a terrace directly on Barceloneta beach.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve a sunbed or cabana at the beach club in advance during August — peak season fills up quickly. Casa Batlló's evening 'Magic Nights' experience is a separate ticketed event and highly recommended for architecture lovers — check if it also has morning or afternoon slots.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to Park Güell — explore Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park with a private guide, focusing on the architectural elements: the Hypostyle Room, the Dragon Staircase, and the mosaic terrace with sweeping city views. Book the first entry slot (8:00 AM) to experience the park in near-solitude before the crowds arrive. Afterwards, explore the Gràcia neighborhood at its base — a charming bohemian district with beautiful Modernista townhouses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau Güell & El Raval Architecture Exploration — visit Palau Güell, Gaudí's early masterpiece and one of his most underrated works, located in El Raval. A private guide can provide deep architectural insight into this UNESCO-listed palace. Afterward, explore the contemporary architecture of the MACBA (Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art) plaza area, designed by Richard Meier.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Nightlife & Rooftop Bar Crawl — second night of nightlife, this time with a curated focus. Begin at Dry Martini Bar (an iconic Barcelona cocktail institution on Carrer d'Aribau), move to the rooftop of the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona for premium cocktails with Passeig de Gràcia views, and finish at a members-style club such as Sutton Club or Bling Bling for Barcelona's sophisticated late-night scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — request a premium in-room breakfast or enjoy the hotel's terrace breakfast with fresh fruit, local cheeses, and Catalan pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Pepita (Gràcia neighborhood) — a beautifully decorated restaurant in a converted pharmacy, serving creative Catalan-inspired montaditos and sharing plates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alkimia — a Michelin-starred restaurant in Eixample offering a refined modern Catalan tasting menu. Chef Jordi Vilà reinterprets classic Catalan flavors with extraordinary precision.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's Monumental Zone requires timed-entry tickets — book the earliest morning slot online. Palau Güell is far less crowded than other Gaudí sites and offers an intimate, genuinely awe-inspiring experience — do not skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Barcelona — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast and take one last stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the Modernista architecture in the morning light. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies (housed in a stunning Modernista building by Domènech i Montaner) for a curated art and architecture experience. Browse the luxury boutiques along Passeig de Gràcia for last-minute gifts — Loewe, Massimo Dutti's flagship, and local design stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: if afternoon flight, check out of the hotel (arrange late checkout if possible — a premium perk worth requesting), enjoy a final lunch, then private luxury transfer to Barcelona El Prat Airport. If evening flight, consider a final visit to the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau — a UNESCO-listed Modernista hospital complex by Domènech i Montaner, often overlooked but architecturally extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Barcelona. If the flight is late evening, enjoy farewell cocktails at the hotel bar or a nearby rooftop before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at Baluard Barceloneta Bakery (if near the waterfront for a morning walk) or at the hotel — savor a full Catalan breakfast with pa amb tomàquet, local charcuterie, and fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Cinc Sentits — a Michelin-starred restaurant in Eixample offering a beautifully crafted modern Catalan tasting menu. An elegant, memorable final meal celebrating the flavors of Catalonia.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — if time permits before departure, grab a glass of cava at El Nacional's champagne bar as a final Barcelona toast.

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout from the hotel to maximize your final morning without luggage stress — most luxury boutique hotels accommodate this with advance notice. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for the airport transfer and security during the busy August travel season.
